ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows a complementary push-pull output stage composed of VT1 and VT2, using a single power supply +Ucc for power supply; the midpoint of the two transistors is the output point C; after point C there is a series coupling capacitor Uc, and the right side of the capacitor is connected to load resistor RL to ground, with output voltage UL marked across the load. Then reason: the problem gives RL=8Ω, and the measured VCC=12V. In order for the single-supply complementary push-pull stage to achieve maximum undistorted output, the static operating point C should be adjusted to half of the power supply voltage, namely VCC/2=6V, therefore after capacitor coupling the maximum sinusoidal output peak value on the load is 6V. Its effective value is 6/√2 V, and the output power P=Vrms^2/RL=(6/√2)^2/8=36/(2×8)=2.25W.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows VT1/VT2 as a complementary push-pull stage with a single +Ucc supply, midpoint output C, a series coupling capacitor, and RL connected to ground as the load. Then use the text values RL=8 ohm and measured VCC=12 V. For maximum undistorted operation, bias C at half the supply, so the maximum output sine-wave peak across the capacitor-coupled load is 12/2=6 V. Convert to RMS, 6/sqrt(2) V, and compute P=Vrms^2/8=2.25 W.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct circuit-topology route: identify the diagram as a single-supply complementary push-pull/OTL output stage and use its maximum symmetric voltage swing limit.
planner_metadata.image_role: From the image, read that VT1 and VT2 form a complementary emitter-follower push-pull output stage powered between +Ucc and ground, with the output taken at midpoint C through a coupling capacitor Uc to the load resistor RL. The capacitor means the load receives only the AC swing around the midpoint bias.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement for the numerical load resistance 8Ω, the measured supply voltage VCC=12V, and the condition that the input/bias are adjusted to maximum undistorted output.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a single-supply capacitor-coupled OTL push-pull amplifier adjusted for maximum undistorted output, the quiescent midpoint C is set near Ucc/2, so the largest sinusoidal load voltage has peak value Ucc/2. Thus Vrms=(Ucc/2)/sqrt(2), and output power is P=Vrms^2/RL=Ucc^2/(8RL). Substituting Ucc=12 V and RL=8 ohm gives P=144/(64)=2.25 W.
